research_rationale:
EO 12261 of January 5, 1981, Gasohol in Federal Motor Vehicles (46 FR 2023, FR Doc. 81-832; published January 8, 1981), was read in full from the held Federal Register text. Issued under section 271 of the Energy Security Act (42 U.S.C. 8871), it requires Federal agencies to specify gasohol as an acceptable substitute in unleaded-gasoline procurements with a preference for gasohol (1-101), allows blending (1-102), sets feasibility and vehicle-designation factors (1-103, 1-104), ties Department of Defense use to section 815 of the Department of Defense Authorization Act, 1980 (1-105), excepts experimental fuel vehicles (1-106), delegates the President's section 271(b) exception authority (1-107), requires agencies to report gasohol usage data to the Department of Energy (1-108), defines gasohol (1-109) and requires implementing guidelines (1-110). The order has no end date. No held instrument amends, revokes or supersedes it: the only held texts that cite its number are its own printing and the 1989 OFR codification; the bounded searches located no later instrument; and the current-law:usc search found the order printed under 42 U.S.C. 8871 and 10 U.S.C. 2922c(a) referring to it by number. All eleven clauses are operative on 2026-10-14. The inventory is unchanged from the dossier (the preamble recites authority and purpose and is not a separate command).
